answer: Identity registration requires a 500-unit stake held against one hardware-bound attestation key, and each key passes a verifiable delay check anchored to the protocol kernel. A sybil attacker therefore locks 500 units per fabricated identity and loses 90 percent of a detected stake after a 30-epoch withholding period. Splitting identities escapes nothing, because per-identity cost stays at 500 units, a single tribunal verdict flags the shared device at every ranked summit, and auditing validators who log the copper-sealed key shares inherit the slash.
